title: "Before the day"
aliases:
  - /tracks/one-day-methods/before.html
---
The day gives the graph, the estimators and the multiverse the time that the other formats give the tools and the practices of open research, and it assumes that a linear model and its output are not new to you. It runs in the browser lab, so the lab opened once is all that it needs from your machine.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) | Open it on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait for the R engine to load (10 to 30 seconds on a slow connection), and run the cell of Task 1. If it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set. | 5 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd) | The original study, its questions, data and selections; SCORE and the Multi100 project; the five reanalyses and an assessment of their choices; and how Multi100 put their results on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case. | 60 minutes |
| [Exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) | The claim and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found. Their recorded partial correlations run from −0.006 to −0.452, and working out how much of that spread comes from the analyses and how much from the conversion of their statistics takes up much of the day. | 10 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), sections 1 to 3 | Why the predictor is measured at the level of the country-year, a first linear model read output by output, and what cluster-robust standard errors repair. Fit the first model in an editable cell of the browser lab. | 60 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Optional. Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure; every fit of the menu then runs live on your machine. | 30 to 60 minutes, once |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) | Pre-reading for Part 4, on what a large set of results together can and cannot establish. | 20 minutes |

**By the start of the day** the browser lab loads on your machine, you have fitted one linear model on the panel and read its output, and you know how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
